title: Seated-vs-Seatless On-Prem Offerings + Timebound SQ Response & Emergency Upgrade Windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a combined experiment to: (1) evaluate customer preference and revenue/ops tradeoffs between seated (per-seat) and seatless (capacity/credits) on‑prem license constructs; (2) produce timebound, templated responses to common enterprise security questionnaires for Private/VPC deployments; and (3) define an operational playbook for emergency upgrade windows and hotpatch entitlements tied to each support tier. Outcome should be a recommended pricing matrix, SQ response template set, and an upgrade cadence policy that can be rolled into sales/legal documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Pricing experiment results documenting at least three customer pilots with preferred structure and willingness-to-pay bands
A set of 6 templated SQ responses (GDPR, SOC2 scoping, KMS/HSM, network segmentation, patching cadence, data residency) vetted by security
Draft upgrade playbook describing major vs minor upgrade windows, emergency hotpatch SLA, and entitlements per support tier
Stakeholder sign-off from Sales, Legal, Security, and Engineering on proposed package and materials

notes: Risk: Seatless pricing may increase operational complexity for deeply air-gapped deployments; mitigation is explicit upgrade windows and paid ops support
Opportunity: Bundling emergency hotpatch entitlement with higher support tiers could increase ARR while reducing churn for regulated customers
